Introduction
FIDE Laws of Chess cover over-the-board play.
The Laws of Chess have two parts: 1. Basic Rules of Play and 2. Competitive Rules of Play.
The English text is the authentic version of the Laws of Chess (which were adopted at the 93rd FIDE Congress at Chennai, India) coming into force on 1 January 2023.

texto:
Preface
The Laws of Chess cannot cover all possible situations that may arise during a game, nor can they regulate all administrative questions. Where cases are not precisely regulated by an Article of the Laws, it should be possible to reach a correct decision by studying analogous situations which are regulated in the Laws.
The Laws assume that arbiters have the necessary competence, sound judgement and absolute objectivity. Too detailed a rule might deprive the arbiter of his/her freedom of judgement and thus prevent him/her from finding a solution to a problem dictated by fairness, logic and special factors. FIDE appeals to all chess players and federations to accept this view.
A necessary condition for a game to be rated by FIDE is that it shall be played according to the FIDE Laws of Chess.
It is recommended that competitive games not rated by FIDE be played according to the FIDE Laws of Chess.
Member federations may ask FIDE to give a ruling on matters relating to the Laws of Chess.

texto_indexado: Article 5: The Completion of the Game - 5.1.2 The game is lost by the player who declares he/she resigns (this immediately ends the game), unless the position is such that the opponent cannot checkmate the player’s king by any possible series of legal moves. In this case the result of the game is a draw.

texto: The game is drawn when the player to move has no legal move and his/her king is not in check. The game is said to end in ‘stalemate’. This immediately ends the game, provided that the move producing the stalemate position was in accordance with Article 3 and Articles 4.2 – 4.7.
artigo_titulo: Article 5: The Completion of the Game
texto_indexado: Article 5: The Completion of the Game - 5.2.1 The game is drawn when the player to move has no legal move and his/her king is not in check. The game is said to end in ‘stalemate’. This immediately ends the game, provided that the move producing the stalemate position was in accordance with Article 3 and Articles 4.2 – 4.7.

texto: The game is drawn when a position has arisen in which neither player can checkmate the opponent’s king with any series of legal moves. The game is said to end in a ‘dead position’. This immediately ends the game, provided that the move producing the position was in accordance with Article 3 and Articles 4.2 – 4.7.
artigo_titulo: Article 5: The Completion of the Game
texto_indexado: Article 5: The Completion of the Game - 5.2.2 The game is drawn when a position has arisen in which neither player can checkmate the opponent’s king with any series of legal moves. The game is said to end in a ‘dead position’. This immediately ends the game, provided that the move producing the position was in accordance with Article 3 and Articles 4.2 – 4.7.

texto: The game is drawn upon agreement between the two players during the game, provided both players have made at least one move. This immediately ends the game.
artigo_titulo: Article 5: The Completion of the Game
texto_indexado: Article 5: The Completion of the Game - 5.2.3 The game is drawn upon agreement between the two players during the game, provided both players have made at least one move. This immediately ends the game.

‘Chessclock’ means a clock with two time displays, connected to each other in such a way that only one of them can run at a time. ‘Clock’ in the Laws of Chess means one of the two time displays. Each time display has a ‘flag’.

texto_indexado:
Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.1 ‘Chessclock’ means a clock with two time displays, connected to each other in such a way that only one of them can run at a time. ‘Clock’ in the Laws of Chess means one of the two time displays. Each time display has a ‘flag’.
‘Flag-fall’ means the expiration of the allotted time for a player.

texto: Handling the chessclock:
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2 Handling the chessclock:

texto: During the game each player, having made his/her move on the chessboard, shall pause his/her own clock and start his/her opponent’s clock (that is to say, he/she shall press his/her clock). This ‘completes’ the move. A move is also completed if:
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.1 During the game each player, having made his/her move on the chessboard, shall pause his/her own clock and start his/her opponent’s clock (that is to say, he/she shall press his/her clock). This ‘completes’ the move. A move is also completed if:

texto: the move ends the game (see Articles 5.1.1, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 9.2.1, 9.6.1 and 9.6.2), or
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.1.1 the move ends the game (see Articles 5.1.1, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 9.2.1, 9.6.1 and 9.6.2), or

texto: the player has made his/her next move, when his/her previous move was not completed.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.1.2 the player has made his/her next move, when his/her previous move was not completed.

texto: A player must be allowed to pause his/her clock after making his/her move, even after the opponent has made his/her next move. The time between making the move on the chessboard and pressing the clock is regarded as part of the time allotted to the player.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.2 A player must be allowed to pause his/her clock after making his/her move, even after the opponent has made his/her next move. The time between making the move on the chessboard and pressing the clock is regarded as part of the time allotted to the player.

texto: A player must press his/her clock with the same hand with which he/she made his/her move. It is forbidden for a player to keep his/her finger on the clock or to ‘hover’ over it.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.3 A player must press his/her clock with the same hand with which he/she made his/her move. It is forbidden for a player to keep his/her finger on the clock or to ‘hover’ over it.

texto: The players must handle the chessclock properly. It is forbidden to press it forcibly, to pick it up, to press the clock before moving or to knock it over. Improper clock handling shall be penalised in accordance with Article 12.9.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.4 The players must handle the chessclock properly. It is forbidden to press it forcibly, to pick it up, to press the clock before moving or to knock it over. Improper clock handling shall be penalised in accordance with Article 12.9.

texto: Only the player whose clock is running is allowed to adjust the pieces.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.5 Only the player whose clock is running is allowed to adjust the pieces.

texto: If a player is unable to use the clock, an assistant, who must be acceptable to the arbiter, may be provided by the player to perform this operation. His/Her clock shall be adjusted by the arbiter in an equitable way. This adjustment of the clock shall not apply to the clock of a player with a disability.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.2.6 If a player is unable to use the clock, an assistant, who must be acceptable to the arbiter, may be provided by the player to perform this operation. His/Her clock shall be adjusted by the arbiter in an equitable way. This adjustment of the clock shall not apply to the clock of a player with a disability.

texto: Allotted time:
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.3 Allotted time:

texto: When using a chessclock, each player must complete a minimum number of moves or all moves in an allotted period of time including any additional amount of time added with each move. All these must be specified in advance.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.3.1 When using a chessclock, each player must complete a minimum number of moves or all moves in an allotted period of time including any additional amount of time added with each move. All these must be specified in advance.

texto: The time saved by a player during one period is added to his/her time available for the next period, where applicable. In the time-delay mode both players receive an allotted ‘main thinking time’. Each player also receives a ‘fixed extra time’ with every move. The countdown of the main thinking time only commences after the fixed extra time has expired. Provided the player presses his/her clock before the expiration of the fixed extra time, the main thinking time does not change, irrespective of the proportion of the fixed extra time used.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.3.2 The time saved by a player during one period is added to his/her time available for the next period, where applicable. In the time-delay mode both players receive an allotted ‘main thinking time’. Each player also receives a ‘fixed extra time’ with every move. The countdown of the main thinking time only commences after the fixed extra time has expired. Provided the player presses his/her clock before the expiration of the fixed extra time, the main thinking time does not change, irrespective of the proportion of the fixed extra time used.

texto: Immediately after a flag falls, the requirements of Article 6.3.1 must be checked.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.4 Immediately after a flag falls, the requirements of Article 6.3.1 must be checked.

texto: Before the start of the game the arbiter shall decide where the chessclock is placed.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.5 Before the start of the game the arbiter shall decide where the chessclock is placed.

texto: At the time determined for the start of the game White’s clock is started.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.6 At the time determined for the start of the game White’s clock is started.

texto: Default time:
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.7 Default time:

texto: The regulations of an event shall specify a default time in advance. If the default time is not specified, then it is zero. Any player who arrives at the chessboard after the default time shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.7.1 The regulations of an event shall specify a default time in advance. If the default time is not specified, then it is zero. Any player who arrives at the chessboard after the default time shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise.

texto: If the regulations of an event specify that the default time is not zero and if neither player is present initially, White shall lose all the time that elapses until he/she arrives, unless the regulations of an event specify or the arbiter decides otherwise.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.7.2 If the regulations of an event specify that the default time is not zero and if neither player is present initially, White shall lose all the time that elapses until he/she arrives, unless the regulations of an event specify or the arbiter decides otherwise.

texto: A flag is considered to have fallen when the arbiter observes the fact or when either player has made a valid claim to that effect.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.8 A flag is considered to have fallen when the arbiter observes the fact or when either player has made a valid claim to that effect.

texto: Except where one of Articles 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 5.2.3 applies, if a player does not complete the prescribed number of moves in the allotted time, the game is lost by that player. However, the game is drawn if the position is such that the opponent cannot checkmate the player’s king by any possible series of legal moves.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.9 Except where one of Articles 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 5.2.3 applies, if a player does not complete the prescribed number of moves in the allotted time, the game is lost by that player. However, the game is drawn if the position is such that the opponent cannot checkmate the player’s king by any possible series of legal moves.

texto: Chessclock setting:
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.10 Chessclock setting:

texto: Every indication given by the chessclock is considered to be conclusive in the absence of any evident defect. A chessclock with an evident defect shall be replaced by the arbiter, who shall use his/her best judgement when determining the times to be shown on the replacement chessclock.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.10.1 Every indication given by the chessclock is considered to be conclusive in the absence of any evident defect. A chessclock with an evident defect shall be replaced by the arbiter, who shall use his/her best judgement when determining the times to be shown on the replacement chessclock.

texto: If during a game it is found that the setting of either or both clocks is incorrect, either player or the arbiter shall stop the chessclock immediately. The arbiter shall install the correct setting and adjust the times and move-counter, if necessary. He/She shall use his/her best judgement when determining the clock settings.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.10.2 If during a game it is found that the setting of either or both clocks is incorrect, either player or the arbiter shall stop the chessclock immediately. The arbiter shall install the correct setting and adjust the times and move-counter, if necessary. He/She shall use his/her best judgement when determining the clock settings.

texto: If the game needs to be interrupted, the arbiter shall pause the chessclock.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.11.1 If the game needs to be interrupted, the arbiter shall pause the chessclock.

texto: A player may pause the chessclock only in order to seek the arbiter’s assistance, for example when promotion has taken place and the piece required is not available.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.11.2 A player may pause the chessclock only in order to seek the arbiter’s assistance, for example when promotion has taken place and the piece required is not available.

texto: The arbiter shall decide when the game restarts.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.11.3 The arbiter shall decide when the game restarts.

texto: If a player pauses the chessclock in order to seek the arbiter’s assistance, the arbiter shall determine whether the player had any valid reason for doing so. If the player has no valid reason for pausing the chessclock, the player shall be penalised in accordance with Article 12.9.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.11.4 If a player pauses the chessclock in order to seek the arbiter’s assistance, the arbiter shall determine whether the player had any valid reason for doing so. If the player has no valid reason for pausing the chessclock, the player shall be penalised in accordance with Article 12.9.

texto: Screens, monitors, or demonstration boards showing the current position on the chessboard, the moves and the number of moves made/completed, and clocks which also show the number of moves, are allowed in the playing hall.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.12.1 Screens, monitors, or demonstration boards showing the current position on the chessboard, the moves and the number of moves made/completed, and clocks which also show the number of moves, are allowed in the playing hall.

texto: The player may not make a claim relying only on information shown in this manner.
artigo_titulo: Article 6: The Chessclock
texto_indexado: Article 6: The Chessclock - 6.12.2 The player may not make a claim relying only on information shown in this manner.

texto: If an irregularity occurs and the pieces have to be restored to a previous position, the arbiter shall use his/her best judgement to determine the times to be shown on the chessclock. This includes the right not to change the clock times. He/She shall also, if necessary, adjust the clock’s move-counter.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.1 If an irregularity occurs and the pieces have to be restored to a previous position, the arbiter shall use his/her best judgement to determine the times to be shown on the chessclock. This includes the right not to change the clock times. He/She shall also, if necessary, adjust the clock’s move-counter.

texto: If during a game it is found that the initial position of the pieces was incorrect, the game shall be cancelled and a new game shall be played.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.2.1 If during a game it is found that the initial position of the pieces was incorrect, the game shall be cancelled and a new game shall be played.

texto: If during a game it is found that the chessboard has been placed contrary to Article 2.1, the game shall continue but the position reached must be transferred to a correctly placed chessboard.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.2.2 If during a game it is found that the chessboard has been placed contrary to Article 2.1, the game shall continue but the position reached must be transferred to a correctly placed chessboard.

texto: If a game has started with colours reversed then, if less than 10 moves have been made by both players, it shall be discontinued and a new game played with the correct colours. After 10 moves or more, the game shall continue.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.3 If a game has started with colours reversed then, if less than 10 moves have been made by both players, it shall be discontinued and a new game played with the correct colours. After 10 moves or more, the game shall continue.

texto: Dispaced pieces:
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.4 Dispaced pieces:

texto: If a player displaces one or more pieces, he/she shall re-establish the correct position in his/her own time.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.4.1 If a player displaces one or more pieces, he/she shall re-establish the correct position in his/her own time.

texto: If necessary, either the player or his/her opponent shall pause the chessclock and ask for the arbiter’s assistance.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.4.2 If necessary, either the player or his/her opponent shall pause the chessclock and ask for the arbiter’s assistance.

texto: The arbiter may penalise the player who displaces the pieces.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.4.3 The arbiter may penalise the player who displaces the pieces.

texto: Illegal moves:
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5 Illegal moves:

texto: An illegal move is completed once the player has pressed his/her clock. If during a game it is found that an illegal move has been completed, the position immediately before the irregularity shall be reinstated. If the position immediately before the irregularity cannot be determined, the game shall continue from the last identifiable position prior to the irregularity. Articles 4.3 and 4.7 apply to the move replacing the illegal move. The game shall then continue from this reinstated position.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5.1 An illegal move is completed once the player has pressed his/her clock. If during a game it is found that an illegal move has been completed, the position immediately before the irregularity shall be reinstated. If the position immediately before the irregularity cannot be determined, the game shall continue from the last identifiable position prior to the irregularity. Articles 4.3 and 4.7 apply to the move replacing the illegal move. The game shall then continue from this reinstated position.

texto: If the player has moved a pawn to the furthest distant rank, pressed the clock, but not replaced the pawn with a new piece, the move is illegal. The pawn shall be replaced by a queen of the same colour as the pawn.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5.2 If the player has moved a pawn to the furthest distant rank, pressed the clock, but not replaced the pawn with a new piece, the move is illegal. The pawn shall be replaced by a queen of the same colour as the pawn.

texto: If the player presses the clock without making a move, it shall be considered and penalised as if an illegal move.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5.3 If the player presses the clock without making a move, it shall be considered and penalised as if an illegal move.

texto: If a player uses two hands to make a single move (for example in case of castling, capturing or promotion) and pressed the clock, it shall be considered and penalised as if an illegal move.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5.4 If a player uses two hands to make a single move (for example in case of castling, capturing or promotion) and pressed the clock, it shall be considered and penalised as if an illegal move.

texto: After the action taken under Article 7.5.1, 7.5.2, 7.5.3 or 7.5.4 for the first completed illegal move by a player, the arbiter shall give two minutes extra time to his/her opponent; for the second completed illegal move by the same player the arbiter shall declare the game lost by this player. However, the game is drawn if the position is such that the opponent cannot checkmate the player’s king by any possible series of legal moves.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.5.5 After the action taken under Article 7.5.1, 7.5.2, 7.5.3 or 7.5.4 for the first completed illegal move by a player, the arbiter shall give two minutes extra time to his/her opponent; for the second completed illegal move by the same player the arbiter shall declare the game lost by this player. However, the game is drawn if the position is such that the opponent cannot checkmate the player’s king by any possible series of legal moves.

texto: If, during a game it is found that any piece has been displaced from its correct square, the position before the irregularity shall be reinstated. If the position immediately before the irregularity cannot be determined, the game shall continue from the last identifiable position prior to the irregularity. The game shall then continue from this reinstated position.
artigo_titulo: Article 7: Irregularities
texto_indexado: Article 7: Irregularities - 7.6 If, during a game it is found that any piece has been displaced from its correct square, the position before the irregularity shall be reinstated. If the position immediately before the irregularity cannot be determined, the game shall continue from the last identifiable position prior to the irregularity. The game shall then continue from this reinstated position.

texto: How the moves shall be recorded:
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1 How the moves shall be recorded:

texto: In the course of play each player is required to record his/her own moves and those of his/her opponent in the correct manner, move after move, as clearly and legibly as possible, in one of the following ways:
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.1 In the course of play each player is required to record his/her own moves and those of his/her opponent in the correct manner, move after move, as clearly and legibly as possible, in one of the following ways:

texto: by writing in the algebraic notation (Appendix C), on the paper ‘scoresheet’ prescribed for the competition.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.1.1 by writing in the algebraic notation (Appendix C), on the paper ‘scoresheet’ prescribed for the competition.

texto: by entering moves on the FIDE certified ‘electronic scoresheet’ prescribed for the competition.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.1.2 by entering moves on the FIDE certified ‘electronic scoresheet’ prescribed for the competition.

texto: It is forbidden to record the moves in advance, unless the player is claiming a draw according to Article 9.2, or 9.3 or adjourning a game according to Guidelines I.1.1
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.2 It is forbidden to record the moves in advance, unless the player is claiming a draw according to Article 9.2, or 9.3 or adjourning a game according to Guidelines I.1.1

texto: A player may reply to his/her opponent’s move before recording it, if he/she so wishes. He/She must record his/her previous move before making another.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.3 A player may reply to his/her opponent’s move before recording it, if he/she so wishes. He/She must record his/her previous move before making another.

texto: The scoresheet shall be used only for recording the moves, the times of the clocks, offers of a draw, matters relating to a claim and other relevant data.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.4 The scoresheet shall be used only for recording the moves, the times of the clocks, offers of a draw, matters relating to a claim and other relevant data.

texto: Both players must record the offer of a draw on the scoresheet with a symbol (=).
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.5 Both players must record the offer of a draw on the scoresheet with a symbol (=).

texto: If a player is unable to keep score, an assistant, who must be acceptable to the arbiter, may be provided by the player to record the moves. His/Her clock shall be adjusted by the arbiter in an equitable way. This adjustment of the clock shall not apply to a player with a disability.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.1.6 If a player is unable to keep score, an assistant, who must be acceptable to the arbiter, may be provided by the player to record the moves. His/Her clock shall be adjusted by the arbiter in an equitable way. This adjustment of the clock shall not apply to a player with a disability.

texto: The scoresheet shall be visible to the arbiter throughout the game.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.2 The scoresheet shall be visible to the arbiter throughout the game.

texto: The scoresheets are the property of the organiser of the competition. An electronic scoresheet with an evident defect shall be replaced by the arbiter.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.3 The scoresheets are the property of the organiser of the competition. An electronic scoresheet with an evident defect shall be replaced by the arbiter.

texto: If a player has less than five minutes left on his/her clock during an allotted period of time and does not have additional time of 30 seconds or more added with each move, then for the remainder of the period he/she is not obliged to meet the requirements of Article 8.1.1.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.4 If a player has less than five minutes left on his/her clock during an allotted period of time and does not have additional time of 30 seconds or more added with each move, then for the remainder of the period he/she is not obliged to meet the requirements of Article 8.1.1.

texto: Incomplete scoresheets:
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.5 Incomplete scoresheets:

texto: If neither player keeps score under Article 8.4, the arbiter or an assistant should try to be present and keep score. In this case, immediately after a flag has fallen the arbiter shall pause the chessclock. Then both players shall update their scoresheets, using the arbiter’s or the opponent’s scoresheet.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.5.1 If neither player keeps score under Article 8.4, the arbiter or an assistant should try to be present and keep score. In this case, immediately after a flag has fallen the arbiter shall pause the chessclock. Then both players shall update their scoresheets, using the arbiter’s or the opponent’s scoresheet.

texto: If only one player has not kept score under Article 8.4, he/she must, as soon as either flag has fallen, update his/her scoresheet completely before moving a piece on the chessboard. Provided it is that player’s move, he/she may use his/her opponent’s scoresheet, but must return it before making a move.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.5.2 If only one player has not kept score under Article 8.4, he/she must, as soon as either flag has fallen, update his/her scoresheet completely before moving a piece on the chessboard. Provided it is that player’s move, he/she may use his/her opponent’s scoresheet, but must return it before making a move.

texto: If no complete scoresheet is available, the players must reconstruct the game on a second chessboard under the control of the arbiter or an assistant. He/She shall first record the actual game position, clock times, whose clock was running and the number of moves made/completed, if this information is available, before reconstruction takes place.
artigo_titulo: Article 8: The recording of the moves
texto_indexado: Article 8: The recording of the moves - 8.5.3 If no complete scoresheet is available, the players must reconstruct the game on a second chessboard under the control of the arbiter or an assistant. He/She shall first record the actual game position, clock times, whose clock was running and the number of moves made/completed, if this information is available, before reconstruction takes place.

texto: If the scoresheets cannot be brought up to date showing that a player has overstepped the allotted time, the next move made shall be considered as the first of the following time period, unless there is evidence that more moves have been made or completed.

texto: Draw offers and event Regulations:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1 Draw offers and event Regulations:

texto: The regulations of an event may specify that players cannot offer or agree to a draw, whether in less than a specified number of moves or at all, without the consent of the arbiter.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1.1 The regulations of an event may specify that players cannot offer or agree to a draw, whether in less than a specified number of moves or at all, without the consent of the arbiter.

texto: However, if the regulations of an event allow a draw agreement the following shall apply:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1.2 However, if the regulations of an event allow a draw agreement the following shall apply:

texto: A player wishing to offer a draw shall do so after having made a move on the chessboard and before pressing his/her clock. An offer at any other time during play is still valid but Article 11.5 must be considered. No conditions can be attached to the offer. In both cases the offer cannot be withdrawn and remains valid until the opponent accepts it, rejects it orally, rejects it by touching a piece with the intention of moving or capturing it, or the game is concluded in some other way.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1.2.1 A player wishing to offer a draw shall do so after having made a move on the chessboard and before pressing his/her clock. An offer at any other time during play is still valid but Article 11.5 must be considered. No conditions can be attached to the offer. In both cases the offer cannot be withdrawn and remains valid until the opponent accepts it, rejects it orally, rejects it by touching a piece with the intention of moving or capturing it, or the game is concluded in some other way.

texto: The offer of a draw shall be recorded by each player on his/her scoresheet with the symbol (=).
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1.2.2 The offer of a draw shall be recorded by each player on his/her scoresheet with the symbol (=).

texto: A claim of a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3 shall be considered to be an offer of a draw.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.1.2.3 A claim of a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3 shall be considered to be an offer of a draw.

texto: The game is drawn, upon a correct claim by a player having the move, when the same position for at least the third time (not necessarily by a repetition of moves):
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2 The game is drawn, upon a correct claim by a player having the move, when the same position for at least the third time (not necessarily by a repetition of moves):

texto: is about to appear, if he/she first indicates his/her move, which cannot be changed, by writing it on the paper scoresheet or entering it on the electronic scoresheet and declares to the arbiter his/her intention to make this move, or
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2.1 is about to appear, if he/she first indicates his/her move, which cannot be changed, by writing it on the paper scoresheet or entering it on the electronic scoresheet and declares to the arbiter his/her intention to make this move, or

texto: has just appeared, and the player claiming the draw has the move.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2.2 has just appeared, and the player claiming the draw has the move.

texto: Positions are considered the same if and only if the same player has the move, pieces of the same kind and colour occupy the same squares and the possible moves of all the pieces of both players are the same. Thus positions are not the same if:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2.3 Positions are considered the same if and only if the same player has the move, pieces of the same kind and colour occupy the same squares and the possible moves of all the pieces of both players are the same. Thus positions are not the same if:

texto: at the start of the sequence a pawn could have been captured en passant.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2.3.1 at the start of the sequence a pawn could have been captured en passant.

texto: a king had castling rights with a rook that has not been moved, but forfeited these after moving. The castling rights are lost only after the king or rook is moved.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.2.3.2 a king had castling rights with a rook that has not been moved, but forfeited these after moving. The castling rights are lost only after the king or rook is moved.

texto: The game is drawn, upon a correct claim by a player having the move, if:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.3 The game is drawn, upon a correct claim by a player having the move, if:

texto: he/she indicates his/her move, which cannot be changed, by writing it on the paper scoresheet or entering it on the electronic scoresheet and declares to the arbiter his/her intention to make this move which will result in the last 50 moves by each player having been made without the movement of any pawn and without any capture, or
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.3.1 he/she indicates his/her move, which cannot be changed, by writing it on the paper scoresheet or entering it on the electronic scoresheet and declares to the arbiter his/her intention to make this move which will result in the last 50 moves by each player having been made without the movement of any pawn and without any capture, or

texto: the last 50 moves by each player have been completed without the movement of any pawn and without any capture.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.3.2 the last 50 moves by each player have been completed without the movement of any pawn and without any capture.

texto: If the player touches a piece as in Article 4.3, he/she loses the right to claim a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3 on that move.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.4 If the player touches a piece as in Article 4.3, he/she loses the right to claim a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3 on that move.

texto: Draw claims:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.5 Draw claims:

texto: If a player claims a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3, he/she or the arbiter shall pause the chessclock. He/She is not allowed to withdraw his/her claim.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.5.1 If a player claims a draw under Article 9.2 or 9.3, he/she or the arbiter shall pause the chessclock. He/She is not allowed to withdraw his/her claim.

texto: If the claim is found to be correct, the game is immediately drawn.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.5.2 If the claim is found to be correct, the game is immediately drawn.

texto: If the claim is found to be incorrect, the arbiter shall add two minutes to the opponent’s remaining thinking time. Then the game shall continue. If the claim was based on an intended move, this move must be made in accordance with Articles 3 and 4.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.5.3 If the claim is found to be incorrect, the arbiter shall add two minutes to the opponent’s remaining thinking time. Then the game shall continue. If the claim was based on an intended move, this move must be made in accordance with Articles 3 and 4.

texto: If one or both of the following occur(s) then the game is drawn:
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.6 If one or both of the following occur(s) then the game is drawn:

texto: the same position has appeared, as in 9.2.2 at least five times.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.6.1 the same position has appeared, as in 9.2.2 at least five times.

texto: any series of at least 75 moves have been made by each player without the movement of any pawn and without any capture. If the last move resulted in checkmate, that shall take precedence.
artigo_titulo: Article 9: The Drawn Game
texto_indexado: Article 9: The Drawn Game - 9.6.2 any series of at least 75 moves have been made by each player without the movement of any pawn and without any capture. If the last move resulted in checkmate, that shall take precedence.

texto: Unless the regulations of an event specify otherwise, a player who wins his/her game, or wins by forfeit, scores one point (1), a player who loses his/her game, or forfeits, scores no points (0), and a player who draws his/her game scores a half point (½).
artigo_titulo: Article 10: Points
texto_indexado: Article 10: Points - 10.1 Unless the regulations of an event specify otherwise, a player who wins his/her game, or wins by forfeit, scores one point (1), a player who loses his/her game, or forfeits, scores no points (0), and a player who draws his/her game scores a half point (½).

texto: The total score of any game can never exceed the maximum score normally given for that game. Scores given to an individual player must be those normally associated with the game, for example a score of ¾ - ¼ is not allowed.
artigo_titulo: Article 10: Points
texto_indexado: Article 10: Points - 10.2 The total score of any game can never exceed the maximum score normally given for that game. Scores given to an individual player must be those normally associated with the game, for example a score of ¾ - ¼ is not allowed.

texto: The players shall take no action that will bring the game of chess into disrepute.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.1 The players shall take no action that will bring the game of chess into disrepute.

texto: Playing venue and playing area:
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2 Playing venue and playing area:

texto: The ‘playing venue’ is defined as the ‘playing area’, rest rooms, toilets, refreshment area, area set aside for smoking and other places as designated by the arbiter.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.1 The ‘playing venue’ is defined as the ‘playing area’, rest rooms, toilets, refreshment area, area set aside for smoking and other places as designated by the arbiter.

texto: The playing area is defined as the place where the games of a competition are played.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.2 The playing area is defined as the place where the games of a competition are played.

texto: Only with the permission of the arbiter can:
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.3 Only with the permission of the arbiter can:

texto: a player leave the playing venue,
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.3.1 a player leave the playing venue,

texto: the player having the move be allowed to leave the playing area.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.3.2 the player having the move be allowed to leave the playing area.

texto: a person who is neither a player nor arbiter be allowed access to the playing area.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.3.3 a person who is neither a player nor arbiter be allowed access to the playing area.

texto: The regulations of an event may specify that the opponent of the player having a move must report to the arbiter when he/she wishes to leave the playing area.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.2.4 The regulations of an event may specify that the opponent of the player having a move must report to the arbiter when he/she wishes to leave the playing area.

texto: Notes and electronic devices:
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3 Notes and electronic devices:

texto: During play the players are forbidden to use any notes, sources of information or advice, or analyse any game on another chessboard.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.1 During play the players are forbidden to use any notes, sources of information or advice, or analyse any game on another chessboard.

texto: During a game, a player is forbidden to have any electronic device not specifically approved by the arbiter in the playing venue.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.2 During a game, a player is forbidden to have any electronic device not specifically approved by the arbiter in the playing venue.

texto: However, the regulations of an event may allow such devices to be stored in a player’s bag, provided the device is completely switched off. This bag must be placed as agreed with the arbiter. Both players are forbidden to use this bag without permission of the arbiter.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.2.1 However, the regulations of an event may allow such devices to be stored in a player’s bag, provided the device is completely switched off. This bag must be placed as agreed with the arbiter. Both players are forbidden to use this bag without permission of the arbiter.

texto: If it is evident that a player has such a device on their person in the playing venue, the player shall lose the game. The opponent shall win. The regulations of an event may specify a different, less severe, penalty.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.2.2 If it is evident that a player has such a device on their person in the playing venue, the player shall lose the game. The opponent shall win. The regulations of an event may specify a different, less severe, penalty.

texto: The arbiter may require the player to allow his/her clothes, bags, other items or body to be inspected, in private. The arbiter or person authorised by the arbiter shall inspect the player, and shall be of the same gender as the player. If a player refuses to cooperate with these obligations, the arbiter shall take measures in accordance with Article 12.9.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.3 The arbiter may require the player to allow his/her clothes, bags, other items or body to be inspected, in private. The arbiter or person authorised by the arbiter shall inspect the player, and shall be of the same gender as the player. If a player refuses to cooperate with these obligations, the arbiter shall take measures in accordance with Article 12.9.

texto: Smoking, including e-cigarettes, is permitted only in the section of the venue designated by the arbiter.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.3.4 Smoking, including e-cigarettes, is permitted only in the section of the venue designated by the arbiter.

texto: Players who have finished their games shall be considered to be spectators.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.4 Players who have finished their games shall be considered to be spectators.

texto: It is forbidden to distract or annoy the opponent in any manner whatsoever. This includes unreasonable claims, unreasonable offers of a draw or the introduction of a source of noise into the playing area.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.5 It is forbidden to distract or annoy the opponent in any manner whatsoever. This includes unreasonable claims, unreasonable offers of a draw or the introduction of a source of noise into the playing area.

texto: Infraction of any part of Articles 11.1 – 11.5 shall lead to penalties in accordance with Article 12.9.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.6 Infraction of any part of Articles 11.1 – 11.5 shall lead to penalties in accordance with Article 12.9.

texto: Persistent refusal by a player to comply with the Laws of Chess shall be penalised by loss of the game. The arbiter shall decide the score of the opponent.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.7 Persistent refusal by a player to comply with the Laws of Chess shall be penalised by loss of the game. The arbiter shall decide the score of the opponent.

texto: If both players are found guilty according to Article 11.7, the game shall be declared lost by both players.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.8 If both players are found guilty according to Article 11.7, the game shall be declared lost by both players.

texto: A player shall have the right to request from the arbiter an explanation of particular points in the Laws of Chess.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.9 A player shall have the right to request from the arbiter an explanation of particular points in the Laws of Chess.

texto: Unless the regulations of an event specify otherwise, a player may appeal against any decision of the arbiter, even if the player has signed the scoresheet (see Article 8.7).
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.10 Unless the regulations of an event specify otherwise, a player may appeal against any decision of the arbiter, even if the player has signed the scoresheet (see Article 8.7).

texto: Both players must assist the arbiter in any situation requiring reconstruction of the game, including draw claims.
artigo_titulo: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players
texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.11 Both players must assist the arbiter in any situation requiring reconstruction of the game, including draw claims.

texto: Checking a ‘three times occurrence of the position’ or a ’50 moves’ claim is a duty of the players, under supervision of the arbiter.

texto_indexado: Article 11: The Conduct of the Players - 11.12 Checking a ‘three times occurrence of the position’ or a ’50 moves’ claim is a duty of the players, under supervision of the arbiter.

texto_indexado: Article 12: The Role of the Arbiter (see Preface) - 12.2.3 ensure that a good playing environment is maintained,

texto_indexado: Article 12: The Role of the Arbiter (see Preface) - 12.2.6 take special measures in the interests of disabled players and those who need medical attention,

texto: The arbiter shall observe the games, especially when the players are short of time, enforce decisions he/she has made, and impose penalties on players where appropriate.

texto_indexado: Article 12: The Role of the Arbiter (see Preface) - 12.3 The arbiter shall observe the games, especially when the players are short of time, enforce decisions he/she has made, and impose penalties on players where appropriate.

texto: The arbiter may appoint assistants to observe games, for example when several players are short of time.

texto_indexado: Article 12: The Role of the Arbiter (see Preface) - 12.4 The arbiter may appoint assistants to observe games, for example when several players are short of time.

texto_indexado: Article 12: The Role of the Arbiter (see Preface) - 12.5 The arbiter may award either or both players additional time in the event of external disturbance of the game.
